stem: How do you solve a sequential game?
choices: Start with the first mover's biggest payoff
Backward induction: start at the last move and work toward the first
Find the dominant strategy in a matrix

stem: A sequential game is usually drawn as:
True or false: Two players who move at different times are in a simultaneous game if the second mover cannot see what the first did.
explain: True. What matters is information, not the clock.

stem: Why does the first mover in a sequential game look ahead?
choices: It always earns the largest payoff
It anticipates how the later player will respond to each choice

stem: A startup launches an app; the market leader sees it and then decides whether to cut prices. What type of game is this?
explain: The leader observes the launch first.

stem: In the slides' Crimea game, who moves first?

stem: Which business situation is best modeled as a sequential game?
choices: Two firms submit sealed bids on the same day
Two stores set prices without seeing each other's ads
A union makes a wage offer and management accepts or rejects it
explain: Management sees the offer before responding.

stem: Can the same payoffs give a different outcome when played sequentially instead of simultaneously?

explain: That is why firms care about moving first or second.

stem: When do a sequential game and a one-shot simultaneous game predict the same outcome?
